title: ADI Qualifying Roadmap
summary: Every step from application to your first ADI certificate, with fees and deadlines, on two pages.

blocks.text: Becoming an approved driving instructor (ADI) takes 3 tests. Part 1 is the theory test: pass it and the clock starts for the other two.

items.title: Apply and get a DBS check
items.text: You need a new Disclosure and Barring Service check to start your application, even if you already have one.

items.title: ADI part 1: theory (£81)
items.text: Multiple choice and hazard perception, booked and taken as a single test.

items.title: ADI part 2: driving ability (£111)
items.text: Pass parts 2 and 3 within 2 years of passing part 1, or you start the whole process again.

items.title: Optional trainee licence (£140)
items.text: After part 2 you can apply for a 6-month trainee licence to get teaching experience.

items.title: ADI part 3: instructional ability (£111)
items.text: A lesson with a real pupil, marked against 17 competences.

items.title: Register (£300)
items.text: Register within 12 months of passing. Then you can charge for lessons.

blocks.title: The 2-year clock
blocks.text: Once you pass part 1, you must pass the other parts within 2 years or you'll have to start the whole process again.

rows: Traffic signs and signals, car control, pedestrians and mechanical knowledge
Driving test, disabilities, and the law
notes: You fail if you score 85 or more overall but less than 20 in any band.

blocks.title: After the test
items: You get the result at the test centre. You must pass both parts.
Pass: you get a pass certificate letter, needed to book part 2.
Fail: the letter shows which parts you didn't score enough on.
Fail: book and take the full test again, at least 3 working days later.
Once qualified: a standards check, registration renewal and a new DBS check every 4 years.
